digest.component_or_area: LLM review operations / CLI command lifecycle
propositions: rebar review is a single-pass unsigned LLM review now superseded from above by the signed review-plan gate and from below by deterministic checks (clarity-check, check-ac, quality-check), and the operator has decided to retire it.

The retirement must be a loud, safe deprecation shim that rejects unsupported arguments (--graph, positional reviewer_id) with exit 2 and error messages naming review-plan as the replacement, rather than a silent alias that would accept and discard them.

The shim must preserve the old verb's read-only, unsigned semantics by forwarding --no-sign=True unconditionally, so scripted callers who ran 'rebar review <id>' still write no attestation (unlike review-plan, which signs by default).

The library function rebar.llm.review_ticket must be split into a private _review_ticket_impl (called by internal harnesses and the MCP tool without warning) and a public facade (emitting a DeprecationWarning) to ensure each user-facing boundary—CLI, library, MCP tool—emits exactly one deprecation signal, not overlapping ones.

Three deprecation registry entries must be created under _ENTRIES with _scheduled() not _permanent(), modeling CLI/lib/MCP surfaces all replaced by review-plan, each with via channel matching its boundary (stderr for CLI, warning for library, log for MCP).

The output schema key 'review' must be repointed from REVIEW_RESULT to PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT, and REVIEW_RESULT re-wired under a synthetic 'review_ticket' key alongside existing synthetic keys ('enrich', 'overlap_judge', 'review_code_gate'), so no schema is orphaned after the shim emits plan-review verdicts.
